subject: Information Theory
title: DNA Data Storage
description: A 60-second lesson on DNA Data Storage.

hook.text: Researchers stored a movie in DNA. It survived for years. Error correction ensured every frame was intact.

buildup.text: DNA stores data in four bases (A, T, C, G). Synthesis and sequencing introduce insertions, deletions, and substitutions.

discovery.text: Reed-Solomon and fountain codes add redundancy across DNA strands. Even if some strands degrade, data survives.

twist.text: DNA can last thousands of years in cold storage. It's the densest storage medium ever: one gram holds 215 petabytes.

climax.text: Error correction is what makes DNA data storage practical despite biology's messy chemistry.

punchline.text: Biology makes errors. Coding theory fixes them.

quiz.question: What types of errors affect DNA data storage?
